utterances.text: Well, you've said that, actually, in your statement, and you've just repeated your evidence. You said you were at Bratunac arranging the funeral of your colleague who died in combat --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Funeral.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Who died in combat; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Even though you heard no shots, saw no Muslims surrendering, captured no one, your colleague died in combat.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: My colleague was killed during the night, and one couldn't see that. I heard shooting. I can't say I didn't. I was woken up by it. They were transferred to Bratunac during the night. I was still not at that place when I learned about it. I called in to see what was going on, and from the Bratunac station they told me to go to the base and that they would tell me then so as not to speak about that over the radio. The next morning I went to Bratunac immediately. I spent some two hours there with the chief - it was Jusupovic at the time - and he told me that he would intervene with my commander, Radomir Pantic, for me to return again to Sandici to inform the men to be withdrawn to Bratunac to prepare for the funeral, which is what I did. So during the night there were no surrenderings and we didn't see any Muslims. When I arrived in the morning, when I returned on the 13th after I had gone to Bratunac, in the meantime, as my people were withdrawing, around a dozen of us, I noticed going from Bratunac to the right, I saw some 50, 60, or a hundred metres away some Muslim civilians, some 50 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, you're repeating the evidence in your statement, but you actually took us a little bit ahead in time to the 13th, and you said you went back to Sandici on the 13th. Now, to get back to Sandici, you actually have to -- from Bratunac you have to drive past the Kravica warehouse, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had to.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: By the 13th, the killings in the Kravica warehouse had already begun. You were driving by, and you saw nothing. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I assert that because -- you need to tell me what time. When I went to Bratunac and returned, it was 10 to 15 minutes, and nothing was going on during that time. What time do you mean specifically, what hour?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What time did you go to Sandici from Bratunac? What time did you return to your men?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, as soon as it dawned, I went to Bratunac. So 5.00 or 6.00 in the morning, perhaps. I told you, I spent two to three hours there. I can't remember exactly off-the-cuff.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So what time did you go back to Sandici to brief your men? On the 13th, what time were you travelling to Sandici?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: You mean when I returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: As soon as I arrived. I don't know exactly, but in the morning. Before noon, that's when I returned to Bratunac. There was nothing going on at the time, nothing of the sort you are talking about. I didn't see or hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I want to know -- we must be losing something, because I want to know what time you went from Bratunac back to Sandici. You went -- you've given evidence that you went to Sandici on the 13th. You went back to Sandici on the 13th. What time did you get there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: You don't understand me, or I don't know. On the 13th in the morning I went to Bratunac. Let me put it this way. In the morning, 5.00, 6.00, a.m., I returned from Bratunac perhaps -- I can't remember exactly, but in the morning, say, two hours later, to Sandici to inform my men to go so that they would go back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So when you got to talk to your men at Sandici, you must have received information from them. Your men must have briefed you about the Muslims who they had captured and collected overnight.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: My men did not receive anyone, and they could not have informed me when they were unaware of it. From my place, Kravica, where I was deployed with my unit, there is at least 1.5 kilometres to 2 kilometres to there. That's the distance. And there's one bend after another, and you can't see from one end to the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I see. We'll move on to another area. Actually, we'll go back in time to Potocari. Now, in your statement -- pardon me. In your statement, you said that after Zeljko's funeral you worked at the station for a day or two, and you don't remember how long before you got sent out again. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it. I don't remember what date exactly, the 16th or the 17th, but in any case, for a day or two we worked and then I received other orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So the strike force was hanging around Bratunac until you got other orders. You don't remember what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: What I was doing while I was in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, regular police tasks for day or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a look -- I want to ask you something relating to that time period, but to do that we have to go back in time. Let's have a look at P4202.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Most probably I also rested. Perhaps I rested. I don't know what I did for the day or two. I rested most likely.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, all right. Maybe this is going to help refresh your memory about what you did for a day or two. P4202 is -- at page 71, now, is a still from a video-clip, and it's a video-clip of you along with your forces, people you worked with entering Potocari from Bratunac on the 12th of July. Now, the people, some of the people identified in this film, have got numbers written on their -- posted on their backs. Number 1 is Milan Milinkovic, who identified himself in this film clip, a member of the 2nd Company -- 2nd Battalion, 1st Company of the Bratunac Brigade. Number 2 is a fellow who was a member of your company, your subordinate, in fact, isn't he? Dobro Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Number 3 -- number 3 has been identified as you. Number 4 is Radenko Tomic, a member of Mauzer's Panthers from the East Bosnia Corps. Now, that's you at Bratunac, and you know these other soldiers -- pardon me, at Potocari, and you know these other soldiers. You worked with them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Incorrect. I never co-operated with these soldiers. You yourself said what units they came from, so we couldn't have co-operated.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You're walking into Potocari in co-operation next to one another with somebody else from your unit. Like I said initially, in a joint force.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No, no. Ninety per cent of the people in the still are my men, but I don't know where the rest come from and how they happened to be there. It's their problem. I never communicated with them. We did not share any command and did not associate.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just let us clarify the transcript. Line 6, did the witness confirm that it was correct? Let us first confirm whether this is the witness himself. Mr. Micic, do you agree that number 3 is yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I'm not a hundred per cent sure, but I'd say that I'm 90 per cent sure that this is me. It's not a problem at all. I said where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It might help just to play a little bit of the video-clip that this was taken from, Mr. Micic, so that you can --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Excellencies, Judge Kwon is right. The witness said that -- didn't say that this is correct. He said it is not correct that he co-operated with those men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That's noted. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We're going to play --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does the witness have the Sanction as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We're going to play P4201, part 2, starting at time-code number 16:45.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] What's up, man? "Slowly. "They need to be told what they deserve. "Just block it and that's it. "Stay, stay. "Pass the word up there. "What? "There, film that ... a trench ... there, up there. "Where? "That hill? "Hello, Goran, if you can't manage it then send those further up there. "A trench? "Let him film the elevation there. "Where did you get the bullet-proof vest? "Slowly. "Do you have the bullet-proof vest? "Old man? I'm taking them down the hill, down there. "Hey. "May I? "Come on, let's go. Let's go immediately. "Shall I take them down the road. "Now move along this way. "Zare. "Nobody will harm you. "Don't be afraid ... come with me ... don't be afraid, nobody will harm you. Don't be afraid. "Come with me freely. Come on. "Nobody will harm you, nobody will. "Don't cry. "We got separated. Please let us reunite. "Don't be afraid. "Why did you leave then? "23 Omega. "Don't wail. Nobody will harm you."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: For the record, I'm stopping the film clip at time-code 18:49.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, having seen the film of yourself and forces around Potocari on the 12th of July, perhaps we can go back to the figures that we looked at in the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: P4202, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Milan Milinkovic, you knew him; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Not well.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: He was --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Perhaps later. No, I didn't know him well. Just by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: He's from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No. He is from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Dobroslav Stanojevic. You knew him; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I knew him. He's a member of my unit. He was my subordinate. I was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Radenko Tomic. You knew him; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know him. He was not a member of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What was he doing with your unit on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Perhaps he was just passing through. He did not have anything whatsoever to do with my unit. We absolutely had nothing to do with him. You're saying "forces" or "unit," but I can see not more than 20 men or even less. What forces are we talking about? How can those be forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, Radenko Tomic, Gargija, he was seen at the Branjevo farm killings, and you know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I haven't a clue. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And for the record, the evidence of that is from Mr. Erdemovic at P332, transcript pages 10974 to 10977, and 10985 to 10986.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not only, Mr. Micic, was he seen at the Branjevo farm killings, he was a shooter. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about that. My unit was not at the place that you mention.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: He came to Branjevo with a group of around 15 others from Bratunac, and you actually know that, too, don't you, and that's why you claim you had -- you didn't know Gargija now.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I've never heard this before. I've never heard that he went to Zvornik with 15 men. I have a vague idea of him, but this is the first time I hear from you that he went there. I can't talk about his whereabouts, where he went, who he went with. My unit was not there. I don't even know where Branjevo is. I haven't a faintest. I was never in Branjevo. Never been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's the day when you say you actually don't know -- you don't remember what you were doing with your unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. These are -- I keep on telling you that I don't know Branjevo. I know that it is in Zvornik municipality. I repeat, my unit was never there. I haven't a faintest where that is. I know where my unit was on those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, then what you were doing on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, I may have been engaged in the Zvornik sector in a place called Baljkovac, but perhaps I was at home. I don't know what date we're talking about. I've already told you that I don't know when it was that I was engaged after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Is it the Prosecution's case in a Mr. Micic was at Branjevo farm participating in the executions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you prepared to answer the question, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: My colleague is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, other than what Ms. Edgerton went through, nothing further. However, just that his statement he has continually said that on the day he doesn't know what he was doing, stories changed about where he was, and he was with at least one person who was determined to be present and taking part, and that's our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency, and I hope I may finish before the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And while we're all looking at this image, Mr. Micic, can you please tell me whether your unit was armed with Zoljas and whether they sported bandannas or kerchiefs on their heads?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: We were a regular unit. We did not hide from anybody. We did what we did in an honest and honourable way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify some things. Can you please tell us whether PJP was your permanent job? Who were PJP members? What smaller units did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No, it was not a permanent position for any of us. We were engaged in combat, and that's the name that we went under, PJP. When we were sent on missions we went as PJPs. When we returned home, we were subordinated to local police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. So when you went back to your regular policing duties, were you a force of some kind?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No. We were not a striking force anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me about the structure of a company. For example, the 1st Company, was that a unit with some cohesion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a unit that consisted of some hundred men, but it was never brought to full strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any smaller units within it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were three platoons, the 1st, 2nd, and the 3rd. I was the commander of the 3rd Platoon, and the platoons consisted or drew strength from the police stations in Birac. I was the commander of Milici, Skelani, and Bratunac police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your men came from those stations; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they received mobilisation calls, they would come from those stations and they would be sent on missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did all the three platoons get to be deployed in the same locality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: It all depended on the situation. It didn't have to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior was Radomir Pantic, the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: His immediate superior, I believe, was the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was your company part of a detachment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. We just called ourselves a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that the only PJP company in the CSB Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No. It was not the only company. My centre in Zvornik had four or five companies in total, and they also went under the name PJP. They were the 1st Company, the 2nd, the 3rd, the 4th, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a unique command for all the four companies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: There was a single command in the centre for all the companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that means that Mr. Vasic could have been your third superior if the single command for the companies, known as detachment, is there, then Vasic would have been the commander of the detachment, right, or the superior to the detachment commander?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's extremely leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very leading. But I do not understand "the third." How come Mr. Vasic was your third superior commander, Mr. Micic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The President asked me who my immediate superior in combat was and that was Radomir Pantic. The second was the commander of all the four or five companies that we had. Danilo Zoljic was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who was his commander?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Danilo Zoljic's commander? It was the chief of the centre, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Dragomir Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From what level did you receive your orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I personally received orders from the level of the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about being captured. You went -- you took your platoon to Sandici. Was your company there, the entire company?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: The entire company arrived in Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you spent the night between the 12th and the 13th there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, the night between the 12th and the 13th we spent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there was not any arrest. Did anybody else arrest somebody while you were there until 6.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: While I was there, there were no surrenders. Nobody was captured. Muslims absolutely did not pass through there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On line 85 -- or, rather, page 85, line 4, you were suggested that you protected Muslims from the Serbian forces attacks.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement provided in 2008, in paragraph 6 you stated that you were protecting them from paramilitaries. What is correct, which of the two are correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Paramilitaries is correct. We were afraid -- or, rather, that was a message conveyed to us from the command to be afraid of retaliation, because one or two years before that, a lot of Serbs had been killed by Muslims, and that's why the command issued us an order in order to prevent any retaliation efforts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was specifically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sorry, before it disappears from our LiveNote screens, a transcript correction at page 102, line 5, Dr. Karadzic is said to have asked the witness: "You were asked about being captured," and I'm sure that's not what Dr. Karadzic would have said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was about people being captured, not about the witness being captured.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank Ms. Edgerton for spotting the mistake in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you captured anybody.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: No. No, President, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, before I forget, just one issue for the witness. You said you were protecting the Muslims from the potential for them being attacked by paramilitaries. Did your forces ever engage the paramilitaries in terms of a stand-off or actual combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were a few incidents in the city involving paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Were you ever personally, or your platoon, ever as a platoon, engaged in such matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never. I was a member of the MUP from 1993, I still am, and I have never belonged to any other units. I was never affiliated with any other unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: No, I'm not suggesting you were. What I was asking was whether either you or any member of your platoon at the time were actively engaged in a stand-off or combat between yourselves and paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During that period of time, no, we did not. I don't remember that we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: At any period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps later, once we arrived in town. There were incidents involving paramilitary groups. There were attacks launched at our station or things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And did your unit or your company suffer any casualties as a result of engagement with paramilitary forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That would be perhaps quite a memorable thing if one Serbian unit of whatever description was attacked by another Serbian unit of whatever description and Serbs were killed by Serbs or wounded by Serbs. You're saying you have no memory of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. There were no casualties, which is why I'm saying that I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Oh, one other --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: What was the company strength, and what was your platoon strength in terms of numbers of men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The company had about 100 men. The platoon should have had about 30, but that was never the case. In practice it was not the case. Some were wounded and were on sick leave. Some were on furlough and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to adjourn as soon as possible. How many more minutes do you need, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Five minutes, Excellency, maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Five minutes, not any more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify one thing. When you say you don't remember, the way I understood you was there was no casualties or that I would remember.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were no casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your task? When you were dispatched at Potocari, what were you sent to do there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: As in my statement, it was to scour the terrain and to come close to a group of Muslims and to provide security for them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am referring the Trial Chamber to the testimony of KDZ084, who said the same thing before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You provided a statement in 2008 as a suspect; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did that status end?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I was a suspect for the case of Srebrenica in 1995. I was suspended for two years. I didn't work. Later on I returned, and the proceedings against me or investigations against me were dropped due to the lack of evidence. And the same was the case with all of the other members who were with me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're no longer a suspect? You were never charged with any crimes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Micic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I have one question in re-cross arising from the questions from His Honour Judge Morrison with regard to paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Further Cross-examination by Ms. Edgerton:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Witness, very quickly. There were no Serb paramilitaries or paramilitaries of any kind in Bratunac in July 1995, were there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. In 1995, I didn't see anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarify just one thing very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About what, Mr. Karadzic? Without putting the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About Ms. Edgerton's question. Let's ask the witness when the police station was attacked by paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly. In 1993, in 1994. I don't know exactly when that was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll stop here. Thank you, Mr. Micic. That concludes your evidence. Thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn here, and we'll continue tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of March, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
